title: Cedar Analytics POC Scoping - Latency & Throughput SLOs
meeting_header: Date: 2027-01-10, Time: 16:00 UTC, Duration: 42m. Redwood: Alex Chen, Priya Desai, Liam O'Neill. Customer: Maya Patel, Ethan Ross, Samir Khan, Rina Lopez.
summary: POC scoping to agree on latency/throughput SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), workload sizing, benchmark plan and timelines. Customer wants p95/p99 targets for both TTFT and TPOT, clarity on measurement methodology and a 3-week POC timeline with concrete success criteria.
topics: TTFT vs TPOT definitions and implications
action_items: Alex Chen: send POC SOW and proposed benchmark spreadsheet — due 2027-01-12
Priya Desai: provide Redwood runbook for TTFT/TPOT measurement and sample scripts — due 2027-01-14
Ethan Ross: share representative traffic samples and prompt set (50k tokens) — due 2027-01-13
Samir Khan: confirm infra constraints (VPC, egress, KMS) — due 2027-01-12
next_steps: Alex to send pricing + SOW and proposed benchmark plan
Schedule kernel-level perf run (Priya) w/ 1B token approx workload
Customer to provide sample traffic and success criteria doc
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh quick intro, I'm Alex the AE, Priya is our SE, Liam is on infra. Maya, Samir, Ethan thanks for making time.
[00:14] Maya Patel: yeah thanks Alex, excited to scope this out. we need to validate latency for our chat and summarization pipelines.
[00:22] Priya Desai: great, at a high level we want to align on two SLO flavors we usually talk about — TTFT (time to first token) and TPOT (time per output token). they have different implications.
[00:34] Ethan Ross: can you clarify TTFT vs TPOT again? i always mix them up in conversations.
[00:39] Priya Desai: sure. TTFT is latency to first token — important for perceived interactivity in chat. TPOT is per-token generation time — important for long outputs and throughput cost. TTFT affects p95/p99 user-experience, TPOT affects sustained throughput and billing.
[00:55] Samir Khan: ok makes sense. for our interactive assistants we care about TTFT p95 under 350ms and p99 under 700ms. Is that realistic on your hosted tier?
[01:06] Priya Desai: depends on prompt size, model, and batching. for a 512-token prompt on a 70B model, on our hosted variant you might see TTFT around 200-300ms p95 with optimized kernels; p99 can be higher due to cold caches and spikes. We can design the POC to measure both cold and warm cache.
[01:25] Rina Lopez: we also have long-form summarization where we generate ~800-1200 tokens. what matters there is TPOT and aggregate throughput — we want to know p95 of time-per-token so we can estimate tail cost and SLA.
[01:38] Liam O'Neill: for TPOT we typically measure tokens/sec for sustained runs and look at p95/p99 of per-token latency across the run. e.g., 50 tokens/sec => 20ms per token average, but tails matter, so we collect p95/p99.
[01:52] Maya Patel: what's your suggested targets for TPOT p95/p99?
[01:56] Priya Desai: for long outputs on dedicated capacity we aim for TPOT p95 around 25-40ms and p99 under 80-120ms depending on model and quantization. on hosted multi-tenant it's a bit higher. We should pick explicit targets for the POC — maybe p95 50ms, p99 150ms as a starting point to validate.
[02:13] Ethan Ross: is that across tokens including first token or excluding first token?
[02:17] Priya Desai: good question — TPOT excludes TTFT. so we measure TTFT separately then measure inter-token intervals after the first token.
[02:25] Alex Chen: i'd like to cover measurement methodology — we'll provide scripts that replay your traffic and produce per-request traces with timestamps for first token and per-token timing. We'll capture p50/p95/p99 histograms.
[02:37] Samir Khan: how do you handle batching in the measurement? our production traffic is bursty but with many short chats, batching will change TTFT vs cost tradeoffs.
[02:48] Priya Desai: we emulate both representative bursty traffic and steady-state sustained throughput. POC plan: two benchmark phases — Phase A (interactive) replays chat workload with realistic inter-arrival times to measure TTFT distributions; Phase B (throughput) runs steady concurrent streams to measure TPOT and overall throughput.
[03:04] Rina Lopez: timeline? we are aiming to decide vendor by end of month, so POC needs to be quick.
[03:08] Alex Chen: understood. proposed timeline: week 0 collect artifacts + SOW, week 1 run initial benchmarks (quick TTFT sweep + kernel profiling), week 2 run full-scale throughput runs and tuning, week 3 validation and handoff. overall ~3 weeks if we start 2027-01-17.
[03:25] Maya Patel: sounds ok. success criteria?
[03:28] Priya Desai: we'll codify success criteria. examples: TTFT p95 <= 350ms and p99 <= 700ms on chat workload; TPOT p95 <= 50ms and p99 <= 150ms on summarization workload; end-to-end cost per 1k tokens <= $X (we'll propose after we see runs); no data exfil on private deployment (if private) and integration compatibility with your KMS and VPC.
[03:50] Ethan Ross: what about measurement noise — how do you ensure repeatability?
[03:54] Liam O'Neill: we run multiple passes, measure warm vs cold caches, capture system metrics (GPU utilization, memory, kernel latencies). we'll also provide the exact replay script and seed prompts so you can reproduce.
[04:06] Samir Khan: for the POC do you recommend Hosted or Dedicated? we have moderate QPS but strong security requirements.
[04:12] Priya Desai: if security is strict and you need VPC/bring-your-own-KMS, Private deployment. For predictability and lowest TPOT tails, Dedicated reserved capacity is often best. Hosted is fastest to try. For POC we can run on Hosted with VPC peering or test Dedicated nodes depending on contract. We'll plan both options in the SOW.
[04:31] Maya Patel: our typical traffic numbers: peak chat QPS ~120, avg prompt length ~400 tokens, responses avg 60 tokens. long-run summarization jobs are scheduled batch: 10 concurrent jobs each producing ~1k tokens.
[04:45] Priya Desai: that's helpful. for sizing, we'll replicate a 150 QPS peak for interactive tests with burst patterns, and for throughput we'll run 10-50 concurrent streams to match your batch patterns.
[04:56] Ethan Ross: what about p99 compliance? sometimes p99 is driven by queuing and OS jitter. do you instrument at app layer?
[05:02] Priya Desai: yes we instrument at the application and host level, collect latencies at the request boundary, and correlate with host metrics. we'll provide dashboards with percentiles and raw traces for problematic outliers.
[05:12] Rina Lopez: regarding cold starts — we have a lot of ephemeral sessions. can you measure cold cache TTFT separately?
[05:18] Priya Desai: absolutely — benchmark plan includes cold-start sweep where we flush caches and measure first-run TTFT. then warm-run sweeps for representative steady-state.
[05:27] Alex Chen: i'll capture that in the SOW: distinct measurements for cold vs warm TTFT and for TPOT tails.
[05:33] Ethan Ross: sample size, how many requests per percentile measurement are you targeting?
[05:37] Priya Desai: we recommend at least 10k requests per workload bucket to get stable p99 estimates, more if possible. for p99 you need tails so 50k is better; for quick validation 10-15k can be okay but noisier.
[05:50] Maya Patel: fine. who runs the baseline? Redwood runs the benchmarks in your environment or we run them against a test cluster?
[05:58] Priya Desai: Redwood runs the benchmark harness by default and shares the exact scripts; if you prefer we can run the harness in your VPC for private deployments. we'll include both options.
[06:06] Samir Khan: what about regional variance? we have EU users mostly.
[06:10] Liam O'Neill: we'll run regional tests — EU region nodes — and note network RTTs. we'll separate infra latency from model inference when reporting.
[06:19] Rina Lopez: are you going to provide cost estimates tied to the throughput SLOs?
[06:23] Alex Chen: yes, one of the outputs will be a cost projection for typical traffic patterns based on measured tokens/sec and batching efficiency.
[06:30] Ethan Ross: ok a few nitty gritty items: does Redwood support KV cache reuse across sessions? that affects TPOT for follow-up messages.
[06:38] Priya Desai: yes KV cache reuse is supported on session pinned variants; we'll measure both with cold KV and warm KV cache. that will show TTFT improvements for follow-ups.
[06:45] Maya Patel: any compliance checks needed from our side? e.g., SOC2 audit evidence to validate logs?
[06:50] Alex Chen: we can share SOC2 report and audit logs info; if you need them for procurement we'll include them in the security packet.
[06:57] Samir Khan: quick objection — we are worried p99 might be non-actionable if spikes come from third-party network. how do we carve that out?
[07:04] Liam O'Neill: we'll include attribution fields in traces (network RTT, infra queues) so we can separate network-induced tails from model-side tails.
[07:11] Rina Lopez: i think we should set two acceptance tiers: baseline acceptance (must pass) and stretch targets.
[07:16] Priya Desai: agreed. baseline: TTFT p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 700ms; TPOT p95 <= 80ms, p99 <= 180ms. stretch: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms; TPOT p95 <= 50ms, p99 <= 120ms.
[07:33] Maya Patel: that seems reasonable. please put those in the SOW.
[07:36] Alex Chen: will do. another point — we'll need sample prompts and a representative production traffic trace (anonymized). Ethan?
[07:42] Ethan Ross: i'll export sample traces and prompts, sanitize PII, and upload to the shared drive by Thursday.
[07:47] Alex Chen: perfect. any concerns about tooling compatibility? for example, we use Prometheus, Grafana internally.
[07:52] Liam O'Neill: we can emit Prometheus metrics and provide JSON traces; we'll share a dashboard template.
[07:58] Rina Lopez: ok, procurement timeline — we need pricing to evaluate.
[08:02] Alex Chen: i'll include a pricing appendix. for the POC we can provide a limited eval credit and run charges will be billable but discounted.
[08:10] Samir Khan: one more technical: do you have an automated measurement for model rollbacks and canary if latency regresses?
[08:16] Priya Desai: yes, Redwood supports canary rollouts and rollback policies; for POC we won't run rollouts but we can demonstrate telemetry that would trigger alerts on SLO violations.
[08:26] Maya Patel: good. let's confirm dates: SOW and benchmark plan by 2027-01-12, sample traffic by 2027-01-13, kickoff 2027-01-17, initial results end of week 1 (2027-01-24), full validation by 2027-02-07.
[08:38] Alex Chen: noted, will send calendar invites.
[08:42] Priya Desai: ok quick recap — POC phases: A interactive TTFT sweeps (cold/warm), B throughput TPOT runs, C tuning and repeat with KV cache pinned, measurement artifacts shared and reproducible scripts. Success criteria baseline + stretch in SOW. deliverables: benchmark report, cost projection, dashboard links, replay scripts.
[09:00] Maya Patel: thanks everyone.
[09:02] Alex Chen: thank you, we'll follow up with SOW and links.
[09:06] [call ends]
